1

 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 02-10-2023.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 02-10-2023 at about 00.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074 on Kuduregere road, near BGS compound, Dasanapura hobli, Bangalore North taluk, at that time the rider of the said motor cycle ridden the in a rash and negligent manner and without observing any traffic rules and regulations suddenly applied break and skidded the said motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Abhaya Vasishta Hospital,
Madanayakanahalli, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and also underwent surgery.

The petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was aged about 25 years, doing coolie work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner lost his income.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- with interest.

3. After service of summons, both the respondents have appeared through their respective counsels,
but respondent No.1 owner has not filed written statement.

The respondent No.2- insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by denying the cause and manner of accident and contended that, the petitioner was not proceeding as a pillion rider and the alleged accident was taken due to the self accident by the petitioner.
Further it has admitted the issuance of policy to the alleged offending Ola Electric Scooter and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further this respondent has contended that, petitioner was not proceeding as a pillion rider in the motor cycle and the said vehicle was falsely implicated in the alleged accident.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied the age, occupation, income of the petitioner.
Accordingly this respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it as the petitioner got injuries due to his self accident.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074 by its Sudeep K M vs Sunitha K R on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199407732/

Further examined Dr. Nagaraj B N, Orthopaedic surgeon at SOADS as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P12 & 13.

On the other hand, the MRO of Abaya Vasista hospital is examined as RW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to R3.
6.
Heard the arguments and perused evidence that are available on record.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;

 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, IMV notice and reply and charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 8.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by the mother of the petitioner.

In the Ex.P1 & P2 they have alleged the negligence of the rider of Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074 and in the complaint they have alleged that the said Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074 was riding by one Sanjay.
In continuation the IO conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P3.

On perusal of Ex.P3, the IO has found the damages in the left side of the body of the Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074 .
10.

The Ex.P4 is the IMV report wherein the Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074 in which the petitioner was proceeding has as a pillion rider has got scratch marks in its left side body at front portion scratched mark.

This shows that the rider of the Ola electric motor cycle bearing No.

sentences.text: No other vehicles are involved in the accident.
As such the negligence of the rider of Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074 is established.

11. It is the main contention of the respondent No.2 insurance company that at the time of accident the petitioner himself was riding the offending Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074 and they have falsely implicated one Sanjay as a rider as the petitioner has no driving license.
In support of the said contention no evidence is placed by the respondent No.2 insurance company.
As per Ex.P1 FIR no doubt that the FIR was registered nearly after 10 days of accident.

But the respondent No.2 insurance company which summoned the MLC register extract which are marked as Ex.R2 & R3 discloses that the petitioner Sandeep admitted to the hospital on 02-10-2023 at about 1.00 a.m. and he was travelling as a pillion rider in two wheeler bearing No. KA.52.V.9074.

Thereby the Ex.R2 & R3 falsifies the contention of the respondent No.2 and helped the petitioner to show that he sustained injuries while travelling as a pillion rider in Ola electric motor cycle bearing No.
KA.52.V.9074.
Thereby the petitioner successfully established his case.

12. The respondent No.1 owner neither filed written statement by denying the alleged accident and negligence nor examined the rider of Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074 to show that there is no negligence from the part of rider of motor cycle.

13. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 by deposing the negligence of rider of the Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074 and produced documents in support of his case to prove the alleged negligence.
The PW.1 was cross-examined at length by denying the negligence of the rider of Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074 but nothing been elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.

Thus, it can be concluded that, the main negligence is on the part of the rider of Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074 who caused the accident by riding the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner.
14. Ex.P8 charge sheet is also came to be filed on one Sanjay K who is the rider of the Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074.
The IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of rider of the Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence from the petitioner and also to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.
15. As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the rider of the Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074.
16.
The respondent No.2 insurance company even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
No rebuttal evidence is placed by either of the respondents.

The charge sheet is came to be filed on the rider of the Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 &
338 of IPC.

At this juncture, I would like to quote the following judgment wherein it states that;

Pushparama and others), wherein it is held that, Certified copy of the criminal court records such as FIR, recovery and mechanical inspection of the vehicle or documents are of sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the rider was negligent.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

17. By relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074.
18.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

20. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by stating that the accident was occurred by his negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.
21. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 02-10-2023 which is caused by the rider of the Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
22.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the rider of respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.

5 a) PAIN AND AGONY:-

entities.text: Sudeep K M vs Sunitha K R

sentences.text: At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 25 years.
As per Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P11 the year of birth of the petitioner is shown as 22-04-1998.
The accident was took place on 02-10-2023.
Hence as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 25 years and 6 months.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P9.

As per Ex.P9 the petitioner was admitted to Abhay Vasistha hospital from 02-10-2023 to 05-10-2023 and he has sustained bicondylar fracture with cannular displacement with impending compartment syndrome left knee (tibia) and also underwent operation for ORIF with LCP and screws.
By considering the nature of injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.70,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bill as per Ex.P10 amounting to Rs.21,000/-.
The medical bill is not seriously disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieve these bill.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding off the same i.e.,
Rs.21,000/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as coolie in private company and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has produced has not produced any documents.
In the absence of any document the notional income of the petitioner is considered in the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P9 - the petitioner was admitted to Abhay Vasistha hospital for 4 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total four months period including 4 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.

So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 4 months =
Rs.64,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner has examined Dr.
Nagaraj B N, Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS hospital as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P12 & 13.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained bicondylar fracture with impending compartment syndrome left knee.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered disability of left lower limb at 40% and whole body at 13%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross- examination.
He has also stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants.
No other expert evidence is lead by the respondents to impeach the credibility of the evidence of PW.2 doctor.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 11% to the whole body.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '18'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 18 X 11 % = Rs.3,80,160/- which is the total loss of future income.

Sudeep K M vs Sunitha K R on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199407732/
6 d) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;

entities.text: Sudeep K M vs Sunitha K R
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Ex.P9 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 4 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P5 the injury sustained by the petitioner is grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injury and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
e) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 4 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

By considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.4,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 4 days in the hospital.

f) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
The petitioner got injuries in his right upper limb and right upper limb.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award him a reasonable sum of Rs. 40,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses:
The PW.2 doctor also opined that the petitioner is in need of one more surgery for removal of implant which may costs Rs.60,000/-.
By considering the same, for the removal of implants, the surgery is very much required hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.50,000/- as compensation under this head.

23.
Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the Ola electric motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.V.9074.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Ola electric motor cycle.
No evidence is placed by the respondent No.2 insurance company to eschew their liability.
No other grounds are made out by showing the contributory negligence of the petitioner or violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence the Respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the liability of respondent No.1- owner.
The petitioner is entitled for the interest @ 6% p.a.

Accordingly,
this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
24.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.6,54,160/- (Rupees Six lakhs fifty four thousand one hundred and sixty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2- insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
